suggestions.msg: typing.Dict is imported but lowercase dict is used throughout the file — inconsistent import style (rule 20).

suggestions.msg: Return type uses Python 3.10+ pipe union syntax (CustomerModel | None) while other files may use Optional — verify project-wide convention.

suggestions.msg: bulk_import builds all ORM objects in memory before flushing — O(N) memory before any DB write; large payloads could exhaust memory (rule 33).
suggestions.suggestion: Consider flushing in batches (e.g., every 500 rows) to bound memory usage, or use executemany-style bulk insert.

suggestions.msg: delete_customer calls flush() even though no auto-generated ID is needed back — unnecessary DB round-trip (rule 36).
suggestions.suggestion: Remove await self.session.flush() from delete_customer — the rowcount check is already done before flush.

suggestions.msg: Explicit async_session.commit() in test body — test code owns the transaction boundary here (rule 121/122 note: tests are exempt, but still worth flagging for clarity).
suggestions.suggestion: No change needed — integration tests own their transaction; just be aware this differs from service-layer semantics.

suggestions.msg: Explicit async_session.commit() in test body — same as line 467.
mock_result.fetchall is a MagicMock (sync) while result.all is AsyncMock on line 31 — if any code path calls fetchall() expecting an awaitable, it will fail at runtime.
suggestions.suggestion: Make mock_result.fetchall = AsyncMock(return_value=[]) for consistency with how the mock is wired elsewhere.

suggestions.msg: session.commit is set as AsyncMock but services never call session.commit() — this mock is dead code and could mask a future accidental commit call.
suggestions.suggestion: Remove session.commit = AsyncMock() from the fixture, or replace with a non-Async MagicMock with a warning comment.
